mainTopic: The laws of שושבינות (groomsmen's gifts), then types of Torah scholars and readings of ״כל ימי עני רעים״
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about שושבינות, the gift a groomsman gives at a friend's wedding and expects back at his own. The גמרא explains each rule: the gift can be collected in בית דין because it is like a loan, it has no ריבית problem, שביעית does not cancel it, and a בכור does not take a double share of it because it is ראוי. רב כהנא then rules that the one who received the gift must repay it even if he missed the giver's wedding. אביי adds how much he may subtract for the meal he did not eat. A ברייתא teaches that the gift is repaid like for like, at the same kind of wedding. The גמרא then turns to a teaching that compares different kinds of Torah scholars to kinds of wealth, and says everyone needs the master of תלמוד. It ends with many readings of the פסוק ״כל ימי עני רעים וטוב לב משתה תמיד״.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא's list of rules for groomsmen's gifts
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its list: שביעית does not cancel a שושבינות debt, and a בכור does not take a double share of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sabbatical Year does not cancel it, and the firstborn does not take a double portion of it.
steps.whatsHappening: We are at the end of a ברייתא that lists the rules of שושבינות. These are its last two rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the ברייתא we learned that the gift can be collected in court and has no ריבית problem. Here two more rules are added. שביעית, which normally cancels loans, does not cancel this debt. And a בכור, who normally inherits a double share, does not get a double share of it.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh (Sabbatical) year, which cancels loans
A double portion of the inheritance
The gift a groomsman gives at a friend's wedding, expecting it back at his own wedding

phrases.english: And the Sabbatical Year does not cancel it,
phrases.notes: "It" means the groomsman's gift that the ברייתא is discussing.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הַבְּכוֹר נוֹטֵל בָּהּ פִּי שְׁנַיִם.
phrases.english: and the firstborn does not take a double portion of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא's list of rules, which began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שושבינות debt is not canceled by שביעית, and a בכור does not take a double portion of it.

steps.title: Why can the gift be collected in court?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now explains the ברייתא rule by rule. It starts by asking why a שושבינות gift can be collected in בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It can be collected in court. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first rule of the ברייתא and asks for its reason. This sets up the explanations that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gift is normally given freely, so you might think the giver has no legal claim to get anything back. The גמרא wants to know why בית דין will force the groom to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: Is collected (by force, through a claim)

phrases.english: It is collectible in court –
what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the ברייתא's rules one at a time
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The legal basis for letting בית דין collect a שושבינות gift

steps.title: The gift is like a loan
steps.stepSummary: The answer: שושבינות is treated like a loan, so it can be collected.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is similar to a loan.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the groomsman's gift works like a loan, so בית דין can collect it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The groomsman gives on the understanding that he will get it back at his own wedding. That built-in expectation of return makes it a debt, like a loan, and not a free gift.
steps.confusionAlert: Saying it is 'like' a loan does not make it a real loan for every law. The next steps show that ריבית and שביעית do not apply to it.

phrases.english: It is similar to a loan.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שושבינות is similar to a loan, so it is a collectible debt.

steps.title: Why there is no problem of interest
steps.stepSummary: Repaying a bigger gift is not ריבית, because the giver did not give with that in mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And it has no problem of interest': because it was not with that in mind that he gave it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next rule of the ברייתא: why a larger return gift is not ריבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the gift works like a loan, you might think a bigger return gift is forbidden interest. But the extra was not given as payment for waiting. It came from the giver's joy at his friend's wedding, so it is not ריבית.

keyTerms.meaning: With this in mind / for this purpose

phrases.english: And it has no issue of interest –
because it was not with that in mind that he gave him.
phrases.notes: "That" means earning extra. The bigger gift was given out of joy, not as payment for waiting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the next rule of the ברייתא after the loan comparison
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An increased return is not ריבית because the extra was not given as interest.

steps.title: Why the Sabbatical Year does not cancel it
steps.stepSummary: שביעית does not cancel the debt, because the verse 'he shall not demand' does not fit this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the Sabbatical Year does not cancel it': because we cannot apply to it the verse 'He shall not demand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why שביעית, which cancels loans, does not cancel a שושבינות debt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about שמיטה forbids a lender to demand his loan. A groomsman cannot demand his gift back whenever he wants anyway. He can only ask for it at his own wedding, so the verse 'לא יגש' does not describe him.

keyTerms.meaning: We read (apply) the verse to it

phrases.english: And the Sabbatical Year does not cancel it –
because we do not read regarding it: "He shall not demand."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the third rule of the ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse of שמיטה speaks of a debt that could be demanded now. שושבינות can only be claimed at the giver's own wedding, so the verse does not apply.

steps.title: Why the firstborn does not get a double share
steps.stepSummary: A שושבינות owed to the father counts as ראוי, and a בכור does not get a double share of ראוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the firstborn does not take a double portion': because it is 'due' property, and a firstborn does not take from property that is due to the father the way he takes from property the father already held.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last rule of the ברייתא using a general rule about what a בכור inherits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור gets a double share only of property the father actually held at death (מוחזק). Gifts still owed back to the father were not yet in his hands, so they count as ראוי. The sons share them equally.

keyTerms.meaning: Property that is due, but not yet received

steps.whatToRemember: The four rules of שושבינות: collectible in court (like a loan), no ריבית (not given for profit), not canceled by שביעית (can't be demanded anytime), and no double share for the בכור (it is ראוי).
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that a בכור does not take a double share of ראוי as he does of מוחזק is a basic principle of the laws of inheritance.

phrases.english: And the firstborn does not take a double portion –
because it is considered 'due' property,
phrases.notes: The father died before the gift was returned to him. It was owed to him, not yet in his hands.

phrases.english: and the firstborn does not take from due property as from possessed property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the last rule of the ברייתא, ending the explanations
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A שושבינות owed to the father is ראוי, and a בכור gets no double share of ראוי.

steps.title: When the gift must be repaid even though he missed the wedding
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא gives the general rule. The one who received the gift earlier owes it back at the giver's wedding. If he knew or should have known about that wedding, he should have come. If he could not have known, the groom (the giver) should have told him. Either way, he still repays.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said, the rule of groomsmen's gifts: If he was in town, he should have come. If he heard the sound of the drum, he should have come. If he did not hear the sound of the drum, the groom should have informed him. He has a grievance, but he must still pay.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא opens a new topic. The man who received the gift earlier did not come to the wedding of the friend who gave it to him. Does he still have to return the gift?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the one who owes was in town or heard the wedding drum, he knew about the wedding. It was his own fault that he did not come, so he must still send the gift. If he was far away and could not hear, the groom should have told him. In that case he has a valid complaint against the groom, but he must still repay the gift.

keyTerms.meaning: The sound of the drum (announcing a wedding)

steps.confusionAlert: Notice who does what. The man who should have come, who has the complaint, and who must pay is the one who received the gift earlier. The one who should have told him is the original giver, who is now the groom.
steps.whatToRemember: In every case the gift is repaid. The one who missed the wedding has a complaint only when the groom failed to tell him about it.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said, the rule of groomsmen's gifts:
If he was in town – he should have come.
phrases.notes: "He" is the one who owes the gift back. It was his own fault for not coming, so he still has to send it.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע קָל טַבְלָא – אִיבְּעִי לֵיהּ לְמֵיתֵא.
phrases.english: If he heard the sound of the drum – he should have come.

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁמַע קָל טַבְלָא – אִיבְּעִי לֵיהּ לְאוֹדוֹעֵיהּ;
phrases.english: If he did not hear the sound of the drum – he (the groom who is marrying now) should have informed him;
he has a grievance, but he surely pays.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא's rules to a new practical rule about repaying the gift
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The one who received a שושבינות gift must always repay it at the giver's wedding. If he could not have known about the wedding, he has a grievance against the groom for not telling him, but he still pays.

steps.title: How much may he subtract?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much a person may take off his repayment because he did not eat at the wedding feast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next move: how big a discount does he get for not eating at the feast?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes that the one repaying, who did not eat at the wedding feast, may subtract something from what he pays back. What is unclear is the amount, so the גמרא asks for a measure.

keyTerms.meaning: Up to how much? A request for a measure or limit

phrases.english: And up to how much?
phrases.notes: He means: how much may he take off his repayment, since he never got to eat at the feast?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the amount of the deduction connected to repaying שושבינות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The size of the deduction for a groomsman who did not eat at the wedding feast.

steps.title: אביי gives the custom for the deduction
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports the custom: up to a זוז he pays nothing, up to four he pays half, and above that each person subtracts according to his importance.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The wedding guests had this custom. If the gift was up to one זוז, nothing is paid back, because what he brought in his hand he ate in his stomach. If it was up to four, he pays half. From there and up, each person subtracts according to his importance.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question with a scale of amounts based on what people were used to doing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a small gift of one זוז, the meal he would have eaten is worth about as much as the gift, so nothing is owed. Up to four זוזים, half is paid. With larger gifts, the deduction depends on how important the person is, since a more important guest would have been honored with a bigger meal.

keyTerms.meaning: Wedding guests, people at the wedding canopy and feast
A זוז, a small silver coin

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The members of the wedding feast were accustomed:
Up to a zuz –
what he brought in his hand, he eats in his stomach.
phrases.notes: A saying: a gift this small is about what the meal is worth, so he owes nothing back.

phrases.english: Up to four – he pays half.
From here and onward –
each person according to his importance.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Up to a זוז nothing is paid; up to four, half; above that the deduction depends on the person's importance.

steps.title: Repay at the same kind of wedding: public and virgin
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a groomsman who served at a public wedding, or at a virgin's wedding, can insist on repaying only at the same kind of wedding.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If he served him at a public wedding and then asked him to serve back at a private wedding, he can say: I will serve you at a public one, the way you served me. If he served him at a wedding to a virgin and then asked him to serve back at a wedding to a widow, he can say: I will serve you at a wedding to a virgin, the way you served me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא teaching that the repayment of שושבינות must match the kind of wedding where the friend was served.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A public wedding and a virgin's wedding are bigger celebrations than a private wedding or a widow's wedding. Since שושבינות works like a loan, the friend can say he will repay in the same form he received it, and not at a smaller event.

keyTerms.meaning: In public, at a large open celebration
In the same way you did for me

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If he served with him in public,
phrases.notes: "Served with him" means he acted as his groomsman at his wedding.

phrases.english: and he asked him to serve with him in private –
he can say to him:
In public I will serve with you,
in the way that you served with me.
If he served with him at a virgin's wedding,
and he asked him to serve with him at a widow's wedding –
he can say to him:
At a virgin's wedding I will serve with you,
in the way that you served with me.

steps.confusionAlert: The one who "can say" is the person who now owes the repayment. He is not refusing to pay; he is insisting on paying back in the same kind of event he received.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another rule about how שושבינות is repaid, building on its loan-like nature.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The one who owes שושבינות may insist on repaying only at the same kind of wedding: public for public, virgin for virgin.

steps.title: Repay at the same kind of wedding: second wife and one wife
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if he was served at a second marriage, or at a wedding of one wife, he may repay only at the same kind of wedding.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he served him at his second marriage and then asked him to serve back at a first marriage, he can say: When you marry another woman, I will serve you. If he served him at a wedding of one wife and asked him to serve back at a wedding of two wives, he can say: I will serve you at a wedding of one, the way you served me.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives two more cases with the same idea: the repayment must match the kind of wedding where the service was given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case the friend says: you served me at a second marriage, so I will repay you at your next marriage, not at this first one. In the second case he repays at a wedding of one wife, not two. In both cases the rule is "the same way you did for me."
steps.whatToRemember: שושבינות is paid back like for like: the repayment must match the kind of wedding where the groomsman served.

phrases.english: If he served with him at the second wife's wedding,
and he asked him to serve with him at the first wife's wedding –
he can say to him:
When you marry another woman, I will serve with you.
If he served with him at a wedding of one woman,
and he asked him to serve with him at a wedding of two –
phrases.notes: This is a man marrying two women at the same time.

phrases.english: he can say to him:
At a wedding of one I will serve with you,
in the way that you served with me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with two more matching cases, closing the topic of שושבינות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Repayment is due only at the same kind of wedding: a later marriage for a second marriage, and a single wedding for a single wedding.

steps.title: Four kinds of Torah scholars
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא compares the master of הגדות, of פלפול, and of שמועות to different rich men, and says everyone needs the master of תלמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One who is rich in property and rich in public fame is the master of הגדות. One who is rich in coins and rich in houses is the master of פלפול. One who is rich in oil and rich in hidden stores is the master of שמועות. Everyone needs the owner of wheat, which is the master of תלמוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic and brings a ברייתא that describes types of Torah scholars by comparing each one to a kind of wealth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each type of scholar has something valuable: the speaker of הגדות is popular, the sharp debater has many "coins," and the one who knows traditions has "stored" knowledge. But the master of תלמוד is like the one who owns wheat, the basic food that everyone must buy. Everyone depends on him because he knows the reasons behind the laws.

keyTerms.meaning: Master of אגדה, the non-legal teachings and sermons
Master of sharp reasoning and debate
Here: deep understanding of the reasons behind the laws

steps.whatToRemember: Every kind of Torah knowledge is valuable, but everyone depends on the master of תלמוד, just as everyone needs wheat.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Rich in property, rich in public fame –
this is the master of homiletics.
Rich in coins, rich in houses –
this is the master of dialectics.
Rich in oil, rich in hidden stores –
this is the master of traditions.
Everyone needs the owner of wheat – this is Talmud.

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is not about real money. The kinds of wealth are pictures for different kinds of Torah knowledge.
steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עַתִּיר נִכְסִין עַתִּיר פּוּמְבֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, non-legal topic after the laws of שושבינות end.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are different kinds of Torah scholars, and all of them depend on the master of תלמוד.

steps.title: רב reads the verse about the poor man as the בעל תלמוד
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא in the name of רב explains ״כל ימי עני רעים״ as the בעל תלמוד, and ״וטוב לב משתה תמיד״ as the בעל משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רב: What does the verse mean, 'All the days of the poor are bad'? This is the master of תלמוד. 'And for the good-hearted it is always a feast': this is the master of משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the theme of the different kinds of Torah scholars. רב reads a פסוק in משלי as describing the בעל תלמוד and the בעל משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, the בעל תלמוד is the 'poor man' whose days are hard, because analyzing and arguing out the sources wears him out. The בעל משנה simply knows and repeats the texts, so for him learning is easy, like a constant feast.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? (opens an explanation of a פסוק)
A scholar who analyzes and reasons through the sources
A scholar who knows the texts of the משנה by heart

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rav said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"All the days of the poor are bad"?
This is the master of Talmud.
"And for the good-hearted it is always a feast":
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same פסוק.

phrases.english: This is the master of Mishnah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of Step 12, which compared types of Torah scholars, by bringing a פסוק that contrasts the בעל תלמוד and the בעל משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'poor man' with bad days is the בעל תלמוד; the good-hearted man with a constant feast is the בעל משנה.

steps.title: רבא says the reading is the reverse
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with רב and switches the two halves of the reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is the opposite.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite reading. For him, the 'poor man' is the בעל משנה and the one with the constant feast is the בעל תלמוד. The גמרא is about to show where רבא gets this view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is one short word, but it flips the whole picture. The בעל משנה is now the one who suffers, and the בעל תלמוד is the one who enjoys his learning. The next step explains the reasoning.

phrases.english: Rava said: The opposite.
phrases.notes: He means: the poor man is the בעל משנה, and the one with the feast is the בעל תלמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's reading in Step 13 and reverses it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'poor man' is the בעל משנה; the one with the constant feast is the בעל תלמוד.

steps.title: רבא's teaching on stones and wood fits his view
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא quotes רבא reading a פסוק in קהלת: the one hauling stones is the בעל משנה, and the one chopping wood is the בעל תלמוד. This matches רבא's reversed reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this matches what רב משרשיא said in the name of רבא: What does the verse mean, 'He who hauls stones will be hurt by them; he who chops wood will be warmed by it'? 'He who hauls stones will be hurt by them': these are the masters of משנה. 'He who chops wood will be warmed by it': these are the masters of תלמוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבא's 'opposite' view in Step 14 fits another teaching of his, on a פסוק in קהלת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who hauls stones works hard and only gets hurt, just as the בעל משנה works hard but cannot reach practical conclusions from bare texts. A person who chops wood gets warmed by the fire, just as the בעל תלמוד gains real benefit from his effort. That is why for רבא the בעל תלמוד is the happy one.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what [so-and-so] said (shows that a view fits another teaching)
One who hauls or quarries stones
Here read as: will be warmed, will benefit

steps.whatToRemember: רב: the בעל תלמוד suffers and the בעל משנה feasts. רבא: the reverse, because the בעל תלמוד gets the real benefit of his hard work.

phrases.english: And this is what Rav Mesharshiya said
in the name of Rava:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"He who hauls stones will be hurt by them;
he who chops wood will be warmed by it"?
"He who hauls stones will be hurt by them":
These are the masters of Mishnah.
"He who chops wood will be warmed by it":
These are the masters of Talmud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up רבא's reversed reading in Step 14 with another teaching of his.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that the בעל תלמוד is the one who enjoys the 'feast'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's reading of קהלת 10:9: hauling stones means the בעל משנה, who is hurt; chopping wood means the בעל תלמוד, who is warmed.

steps.title: רבי חנינא reads the verse as about a bad wife and a good wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא explains the 'poor man' as someone with a bad wife, and the good-hearted man as someone with a good wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: 'All the days of the poor are bad': this is someone who has a bad wife. 'And for the good-hearted it is always a feast': this is someone who has a good wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves away from Torah scholars and brings other readings of the same פסוק in משלי. רבי חנינא applies it to married life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי חנינא, the פסוק is about home life. A bad wife makes every day hard, and a good wife makes life feel like a constant feast. This starts a list of different readings of the same פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: ״כׇּל יְמֵי עָנִי רָעִים״ –
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said: "All the days of the poor are bad":
this is one who has a bad wife.
"And for the good-hearted it is always a feast":
this is one who has a good wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: ״כׇּל יְמֵי עָנִי רָעִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the scholar-based readings and starts a list of other readings of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bad wife makes all one's days bad; a good wife makes life a constant feast.

steps.title: רבי ינאי reads the verse as about an overly sensitive person and a relaxed one
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי explains the 'poor man' as an overly sensitive person (איסטניס), and the good-hearted man as an easygoing person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: 'All the days of the poor are bad': this is a delicate, overly sensitive person. 'And for the good-hearted it is always a feast': this is someone who is easygoing.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא reads the same פסוק. רבי ינאי applies it to personality: a fussy person versus a relaxed one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The איסטניס is bothered by everything around him, so every day feels bad. A person whose mind is settled and easygoing is content with what he has, so life is like a feast.

keyTerms.meaning: A delicate, fussy, overly sensitive person

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמַר: ״כׇּל יְמֵי עָנִי רָעִים״ –
phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said: "All the days of the poor are bad":
this is a delicate, overly sensitive person.
"And for the good-hearted it is always a feast":
this is one who is easygoing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמַר: ״כׇּל יְמֵי עָנִי רָעִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another reading of the same פסוק to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An overly sensitive person suffers every day; an easygoing person always feels he is at a feast.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן reads the verse as about a compassionate person and a cruel one
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains the 'poor man' as a compassionate person (רחמן), and the one with the constant feast as a cruel person (אכזרי).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: 'All the days of the poor are bad': this is a compassionate person. 'And for the good-hearted it is always a feast': this is a cruel person.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a surprising reading of the same פסוק: the compassionate person is the one whose days are bad, and the cruel person is the one who feasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A compassionate person feels other people's pain, so his days are filled with sorrow. A cruel person is not moved by anyone's suffering, so he goes on enjoying himself. This does not mean the פסוק praises cruelty; it describes how each one feels.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying cruelty is good. רבי יוחנן is only describing who feels pain and who does not.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: ״כׇּל יְמֵי עָנִי רָעִים״ –
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: "All the days of the poor are bad":
this is a compassionate person.
"And for the good-hearted it is always a feast":
this is a cruel person.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: ״כׇּל יְמֵי עָנִי רָעִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another reading of the same פסוק to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The compassionate person suffers all his days; the cruel person always feasts.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי reads the verse as about an impatient person and a patient one
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי explains the 'poor man' as an impatient person, and the good-hearted man as a patient, broad-minded person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: 'All the days of the poor are bad': this is someone with a short temper. 'And for the good-hearted it is always a feast': this is someone with a patient, broad mind.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last reading in the list. רבי יהושע בן לוי applies the פסוק to patience versus impatience.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person with a 'short mind' gets upset easily, so every day feels bad. A person with a 'wide mind' takes things calmly, so his life is like a constant feast.
steps.whatToRemember: The same פסוק, ״כל ימי עני רעים וטוב לב משתה תמיד״, is read in many ways: בעל תלמוד versus בעל משנה (רב and רבא disagree), a bad versus a good wife, fussy versus easygoing, compassionate versus cruel, and impatient versus patient.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
"All the days of the poor are bad":
this is one who is impatient.
"And for the good-hearted it is always a feast":
this is one who is patient.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר: ״כׇּל יְמֵי עָנִי רָעִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the list of readings of the same פסוק.
